#### What this PR does / why we need it: 
When memory requests are resized, we must invoke UpdateContainerResources or trigger container stop/start (if RestartContainer resize policy is in force) in order to update the oom_score_adj (and perhaps resize memory.min ... in the future, under memoryQoS feature-gate). This omission was an oversight in my initial implementation, and this PR fixes it.

issue_context.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Memory request resizing should be acted on
issue_context.body:
Currently we don't actuate memory request resizes through the runtime, since memory requests aren't directly configured through cgroups. However, memory requests are indirectly configured through `OomScoreAdj`, and if MemoryQoS is enabled through `memory.high` (also swap, but that needs it's own separate discussion).

We should start issuing `UpdateContainerResources` requests for memory request resizing.

**Open question:** Should we restart the container if the memory restart policy is `RestartContainer`, but only the request is resizing? I think yes. Even if it doesn't seem necessary for OomScoreAdj, it might be for setting `memory.high`, and is generally more consistent.

/sig node
/priority important-soon
/triage accepted
/cc @esotsal @dchen1107 @vinaykul
comments: I'd like to take this issue and give it a try this weekend.

@Karthik-K-N pointed out that runc does not actually update `oom_score_adj`, in https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/4669.

I still think we want to make this change anyway, and hopefully we can get it patched in runc.
Long back I tried similar [thing](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121218) and I think lots of things changed since then.

Hi, I've been testing `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` on a locally built Kubernetes cluster using both `kind` and `minikube`. I enabled the feature gate, but `kubectl patch` still fails with:

```
The Pod "inplacedemo" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: pod updates may not change fields other than ...
```

This happens when I try to increase CPU limits or memory requests.

### **I Tried...**
- **Built Kubernetes from source** (following @vinaykul 's work)
- **Enabled feature gate everywhere:**
  - **kind:** 
```
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
name: dev-cluster
featureGates:
  MemoryQoS: true
  InPlacePodVerticalScaling: true
nodes:
  - role: control-plane
    image: kindest/node:latest
    kubeadmConfigPatches:
      - |
        apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
        kind: ClusterConfiguration
        metadata:
          name: config
        apiServer:
          extraArgs:
            feature-gates: "MemoryQoS=true,InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true"
        controllerManager:
          extraArgs:
            feature-gates: "MemoryQoS=true,InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true"
        scheduler:
          extraArgs:
            feature-gates: "MemoryQoS=true,InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true"
  - role: worker
    image: kindest/node:latest
    kubeadmConfigPatches:
      - |
        apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
        kind: InitConfiguration
        nodeRegistration:
          kubeletExtraArgs:
            feature-gates: "MemoryQoS=true,InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true"

```
  - **kube-apiserver args:** Confirmed `--feature-gates=MemoryQoS=true,InPlacePodVerticalScaling=true`
  - **kubelet config.yaml:** Confirmed in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`
```
featureGates:
  InPlacePodVerticalScaling: true
  MemoryQoS: true
```
- **Pod YAML:**

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: inplacedemo
spec:
  containers:
  - name: inplacedemo
    image: alpine
    command: ["tail", "-f", "/dev/null"]
    resizePolicy:
    - resourceName: "memory"
      restartPolicy: "RestartContainer"
    - resourceName: "cpu"
      restartPolicy: "NotRequired"
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 2
        memory: "1Gi"
      requests:
        cpu: 1
        memory: "500Mi"
  ```

- **Tested CPU resize:**
  ```sh
  kubectl patch pod inplacedemo --patch '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"inplacedemo", "resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"3"}}}]}}'
  ```
  **Got validation error:**
  ```
  The Pod "inplacedemo" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: pod updates may not change fields other than ...
  ```

### **What I Expected**
- `kubectl patch` should allow in-place resizing if the feature gate is enabled. As demonstrated in this blog: [[this blog](https://medium.com/@karla.saur/trying-out-the-new-in-place-pod-resource-resizing-68a0b3c42b72)](https://medium.com/@karla.saur/trying-out-the-new-in-place-pod-resource-resizing-68a0b3c42b72)
- `kubectl get pod inplacedemo -o yaml` should show `allocatedResources` and `resize` fields.

### **Questions**
1. Am I missing another flag or config?
2. Has the behavior changed since 1.27? (Following [[this blog](https://medium.com/@karla.saur/trying-out-the-new-in-place-pod-resource-resizing-68a0b3c42b72)](https://medium.com/@karla.saur/trying-out-the-new-in-place-pod-resource-resizing-68a0b3c42b72))

Thanks in advance!

Yes, patch command in the medium article is not valid any longer and will need to be updated after beta graduation, https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/50024 and updated documentation will improve things.
